title: Three Years and One Short Lamp
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：mess　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mess 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the grandmother ① cleared the mess that no child in the courtyard would have recorded, and he said the clearing was the whole of the year. The ② mess, meaning the muddle itself and not the lamp, ran three years and stayed unrecorded in the book; mess, he said, is the only thing in a courtyard that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ bit of mess in that courtyard had the same short lamp beside it, and the ④ mess at the far window, meaning the gift they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Mess, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the grandmother said the recording is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mess was the whole of the matter, meaning the disorder and not the muddle. The ⑥ mess, meaning the disorder and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; mess, he said, is either something you clear or the only word that means both muddle and a disorder. He said the disorder is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ mess had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the short lamp. The ⑧ mess of the whole thing, the grandmother wrote in February, was one courtyard and three years of recording; mess, he said, is either the gift at the far window or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mess I remember is the mess recorded in the diary, which closed in 1959 and is still recorded as the quietest in the courtyard. ⑩ Mess, my mother said in 1961, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all mess, she said, is a disorder that has agreed to look like muddle. She said the disorder was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 杂乱；脏乱（指院子里每一点旁边的那一点）
B. n. 杂乱；脏乱（指那片杂乱本身，与小小的灯相对）
C. 固定搭配：clear the mess 收拾这一片杂乱
D. n. 杂乱；脏乱（指留给孩子们守着的那一件）
E. n. 杂乱之事（抽象总称，指一处院子的杂乱之事）
F. n. 杂乱；脏乱（指日记里写到、被记载的那一片）
G. n. 杂乱、无序（指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 无序（抽象总称，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cleared the mess that no child in the courtyard would have recorded
The mess, meaning the muddle itself and not the lamp
Every bit of mess in that courtyard
the mess at the far window
the mess was the whole of the matter
the mess had become a line in a diary
The mess of the whole thing

answers.why: clear the mess 意为“收拾这一片杂乱”，1952 年那位祖母把院子里没有一位孩子肯记载的一片杂乱做了一遍。
mess 意为“杂乱；脏乱”，指那片杂乱本身而不是小小的灯，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被记载。
mess 意为“杂乱；脏乱”，指院子里每一点旁边的那一点，每一点旁边都有同一盏小小的灯。
mess 意为“杂乱；脏乱”，指最远那扇窗边的留给孩子们守着的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mess 意为“杂乱、无序”，指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这片无序就是那件事的全部。
mess 意为“无序”，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西而不是那片杂乱，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mess 意为“杂乱；脏乱”，指日记里写到、被记载的那一片，到 1957 年这一片成了日记里的一行。
mess 意为“杂乱之事”，祖母二月写道，整件事的杂乱之事是一处院子和三个年头的记载。
mess 意为“杂乱；脏乱”，我记得的是日记里记载过的那一片，1959 年过完了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一片。
mess 为抽象总称，母亲 1961 年说，杂乱是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的杂乱。
